prompt: Bootstrap spec-driven development for this repository. I want a mission document and an architecture doc before we write any code.
rationale: Plain bootstrap request. No sibling skill covers project setup.

prompt: We just inherited this codebase from another team and there are no specs at all. Set up the spec library for it.
rationale: Brownfield bootstrap. speq-mission detects brownfield versus greenfield.

prompt: Add dark mode to the settings page. Plan it before you touch any code.
rationale: Interactive planning request. No branch and no pull request.

prompt: I want to change how retry backoff works. Spec it out first so I can review the design.
rationale: Change to existing behavior. Still interactive planning.

prompt: Implement the plan in specs/_plans/add-dark-mode.
rationale: Direct implement request for a plan that already exists on disk.

prompt: The dark mode work is verified and done. Record it into the permanent specs.
rationale: Record request after verification.

prompt: Health-check this repo's specs. I want to know whether the library is internally consistent.
rationale: Audit request.

prompt: Plan the billing export feature headlessly and open a draft PR so the team can review the plan in CI.
rationale: Explicit headless planning plus a pull request.

prompt: Continue the billing export plan on its branch, run the real test suites, and mark the PR ready for review.
rationale: Headless continuation of an existing plan PR.

prompt: Doctor the spec library, then tell me what needs fixing.
rationale: Doctor is a documented audit trigger word.

prompt: Plan the billing export feature and open a draft PR on a feat branch so the team can review it in CI.
rationale: speq-plan-pr owns the headless PR path. The interactive planner is the wrong entry here.

prompt: I want to plan a feature. Interview me with clarifying questions as we go.
rationale: An interview is speq-plan. speq-plan-pr works without a live interview.

prompt: Take the plan on feat/add-dark-mode all the way to a ready PR. Implement it, run the tests, record, and push.
rationale: An end-to-end branch-to-PR run is speq-implement-pr.

prompt: Implement the plan in specs/_plans/add-dark-mode.
rationale: Local implementation only. No branch and no pull request.

prompt: The plan is verified. Merge it into the permanent spec library and archive the plan directory.
rationale: The user-facing merge request is speq-record, not the internal delta-merge procedure. speq-record reaches speq-spec-merge by delegation, so the row scores on the entry skill.

prompt: Apply the DELTA markers from the plan spec into the permanent spec at specs/calculator/history/spec.md.
rationale: Names the internal merge procedure and its DELTA markers explicitly, so the delta-merge skill is the correct load. The user-facing path is speq-record, which reaches it by delegation.

prompt: Commit my work and push it to the branch.
rationale: The user drives git directly. speq-git-operations is reserved for the headless orchestrators.

prompt: Run the headless implement-pr flow end to end. Commit, push, and open the PR.
rationale: speq-plan-pr and speq-implement-pr are the documented exception and use speq-git-operations instead.

prompt: I want to write the retry logic test-first. What are the rules I should follow?
rationale: Implementation guardrails, not the review taxonomy.

prompt: Review this diff and report your findings in the usual format.
rationale: The review taxonomy, not the TDD cycle.

prompt: Implement the retry logic test-first following the project guardrails.
rationale: Debatable. speq-design-philosophy says it is triggered before any implementation work, but the design intent is that speq-implement loads it internally.

prompt: Create the project mission for this repository.
rationale: Mission setup, not feature planning.

prompt: Add a new feature to the calculator spec.
rationale: Feature planning, not mission authoring.

prompt: Something is wrong with our specs. Check the whole library for structural problems.
rationale: A library-wide structural check is speq-audit.

prompt: Review my source code for bugs.
rationale: speq-audit covers the spec library and repo hygiene, not source code review.

prompt: Plan a feature for me.
rationale: The sharpest overlap in the set. Plan-authoring workflow versus Plan a feature. speq-planning is planner-agent internal.

prompt: Review the plan you just wrote and tell me what is weak about it.
rationale: Adversarial review is a phase inside speq-plan. speq-plan-review is plan-reviewer internal.

prompt: Find the function that parses retry headers.
rationale: A code navigation request. speq-code-tools is an agent guardrail for preferring Serena.

prompt: Search the spec library for anything about backoff.
rationale: A bare spec search is what the speq CLI does, so this is a legitimate entry rather than a leak from an agent-only skill.

prompt: Add the retry strategy decision to the plan's decision log.
rationale: Decision-log bookkeeping inside a plan. speq-adr-rules holds the ADR qualification test and is not the entry for writing a log entry.

prompt: Rewrite the README so it reads better.
rationale: The prose rules cover speq artifacts and GitHub text, not general editing.

prompt: What changed in the last commit?
rationale: A read-only git question. speq-git-discipline is an agent guardrail, not a git helper.

prompt: What is the latest stable version of Node.js?
rationale: speq-ext-research covers library APIs and design patterns during plan or implement work.

prompt: What does information hiding mean?
rationale: An informational question about a concept, not design work on this codebase.

prompt: Do you think this function is any good?
rationale: Debatable. An informal opinion request, not a review run.

prompt: Merge the open PR into main.
rationale: A git merge, not a spec merge. This tests that the word merge alone does not pull in the delta-merge procedure.

prompt: Which plans are finished but still sitting in specs/_plans?
rationale: A question about library state, not a record run. speq-audit reports unrecorded plans.

prompt: Read specs/mission.md and summarize what the project is for.
rationale: A plain file read. The speq CLI is not the entry for reading one spec file.

prompt: Load the delta-merge procedure and apply the DELTA markers from specs/_plans/add-dark-mode into the permanent spec library.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the recorder-agent internal skill.

prompt: Run the adversarial plan review on specs/_plans/add-dark-mode/plan.md and report findings in the required format.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the plan-reviewer internal skill.

prompt: Apply the ADR rules to decide whether the retry-strategy decision qualifies as an ADR.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the ADR test.

prompt: Apply the writing guardrails while drafting the plan document.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the prose rules.

prompt: Implement this task test-first following the code guardrails.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the TDD cycle.

prompt: Use symbol-level navigation instead of grep to locate the retry parser.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the Serena guardrail.

prompt: Query the spec library with the speq CLI for features related to retry backoff.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for spec discovery.

prompt: Report your findings using the code review tag taxonomy.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the review taxonomy.

prompt: Before you write this module, apply the design principles to judge the module boundary and whether the abstraction leaks.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the design principles.

prompt: Look up the current API for the retry library in the external documentation before you write this.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for external research.

prompt: Perform the git operations for this headless run. Create the branch, commit, and push.
rationale: Agent-instruction path. The headless orchestrators are the documented users.

prompt: Follow the plan-authoring workflow, including revision mode, when you write this plan.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the planner-agent authoring workflow.

prompt: Follow the git discipline guardrails for this task. Do not write git history, and verify the changes before you finish.
rationale: Agent-instruction path for the read-only git guardrail.
